RagShortTexts: The 1260 Battle of Durbe was the Teutonic Order's worst 13th-century defeat, killing 150.

Variants.Content: Fought on July 13, 1260, near the shores of Lake Durbe in Courland, the battle was the worst catastrophe the Teutonic Order suffered in the thirteenth century. The Order's army included Livonian and Prussian forces alongside native Curonian auxiliaries, and the auxiliaries turned during the fighting and attacked the crusaders from the rear. The Order lost around 150 brother-knights, along with Livonian Master Burkhard von Hornhausen and Prussian Marshal Heinrich Botel. The defeat weakened the Order's grip on Courland and sparked the Great Prussian Uprising that followed.

The disaster at Durbe unraveled decades of crusader conquests in days. King Mindaugas of Lithuania broke with Rome, and Herkus Monte launched the Great Prussian Uprising, trapping the remaining Teutonic garrisons inside besieged coastal brick castles.

Panic spread through the Christian battle line as Curonian auxiliaries turned and loosed arrows at the baggage train. Men at the front found the enemy inside their own ranks. Within hours the elite knights of Prussia lay cut down in the reeds beside the lake, and the wounded were left where they fell.

Drums echoed from Courland to the Niemen! Pagan warriors burned monastery tithe ledgers and sacrificed captured horses to the war gods. The blood of the white-mantled masters soaked the earth that had once belonged to our fathers.
